entry.title: Remaking the site: Hakimacs to Kenbun
entry.content:
In January I wrote about Revamp the blogs and in march about Replenish theme - its Emacsy. Now, here we go once more. Same same, but really different

The old look, Hakimacs, painted every page as an Emacs window: a menu bar on top, a modeline at the bottom, an echo area, dropdowns, frosted glass. I loved how it looked. But over time I kept adding "helpers for reading" and now the helpers look noisier than the reading. I like how Bear Blog, Miniflux Lobsters just let you read, with no BS. So this time the rule was simple: the page exists to be read, and the CSS exists to be maintained.

The new look is Kenbun, named after Kenbunshoku Haki, the observation Haki (its all One Piece-d). Sense what matters, drop the noise.

Before and after#

Before: the home page as an Emacs window, with menu bar and modeline

After: the home page in Kenbun, title, links and a plain column

Before: the posts listing page

After: the new simple listing page

Before: a post inside the Emacs frame

After: the same post, just the words

What went#

  • The fake Emacs frame: menu bar, modeline, echo area, hamburger menu.
  • Breadcrumbs, the reading progress bar, sidenotes, code copy buttons, the image lightbox.
  • A random colour scheme on every visit, the themes gallery, and the rain confetti on badges.

What stayed, because I want it#

  • My fonts, the heading glyphs, and the five font modes.
  • base16 colour schemes, with Haki as the default.
  • The command palette with its glass blur, one place to search and navigate everything.
  • The spinning glow on hover, the badges, and the WANTED poster on the 404 page.

By the numbers#

File Before After
theme.css 3365 915
index.js 1436 822
theme.el 1219 565

What I kept in mind#

  • Style plain HTML elements first, and keep a short list of shared pieces. A new page reuses them; it never gets its own CSS.
  • Trust the browser: <details> for folding, <dialog> for the palette, a popover for small notes.
  • Readable or gone. Every colour scheme is checked for contrast when the site is built, and only 140 pass AAA out of 306 schemes.

Read more, write more, give more
